detail.abstract: This review critiques John Y. Campbell and Tarun Ramadorai's book Fixed: Why Personal Finance Is Broken and How to Make It Work for Everyone (2025), which argues that the financial system is systematically tilted against unsophisticated investors, perpetuating inequality and increasing cynicism among the public that financial markets cheat the "little guys". While the book offers a compelling synthesis of modern household behavioral finance, I argue that it reflects a deeper conceptual limitation within the field: the tendency to treat household capabilities as fixed. In contrast, I present an alternative model of lifetime skill development that emphasizes the role that human capital acquisition plays in shaping one's financial decision-making ability. Such skill formation is produced through investing time and effort over the life-cycle. The policy implications of how to help lower income people to achieve their goals in financial markets crucially depend on whether individuals can develop the skills to navigate these markets on their own or whether (as the authors claim) ex-post paternalistic safeguards are needed. Behavioral household finance has documented that people make systematic mistakes. Rational expectations economists model people as learning from their mistakes and having some humility in anticipating that they will make more mistakes if they don't invest in skill acquisition. This forward looking life-cycle investment helps them to adapt to challenges in all markets including financial markets.

title:
Between Disclosure and Conspiracy:
The Transparency Effect on r/UFO and r/UAP Subreddits
affiliations: University College Dublin and Arizona State University (ASU)

detail.title:
Between Disclosure and Conspiracy:
The Transparency Effect on r/UFO and r/UAP Subreddits
detail.abstract: While there exists genuine scientific inquiry seeking to understand Unidentified Anomalous Phenomena (UAPs), the lore of Unidentified Flying Objects (UFOs) is deeply intertwined with narratives deliberately crafted to mislead, obfuscate, and manipulate public perception with a community historically targeted by sustained disinformation campaigns. In this study, we explore the public reception regarding UAP disclosures against the historical context of government disinformation and obstructive information flows. To this end, we retrieved the posts and comments featured in the UAP and UFO Reddit communities and modeled the data by constructing a timeline of governmental and intelligence announcements, leaks, and reports, but also congressional and senate committee hearings, special news reports, and DOD AARO public statements about UAPs. Using time series analysis techniques, we modeled this data to test whether government direct engagement with the topic has tangible effects in subsiding disinformation concerns and conspiratorial narratives within these communities. Our results show that the transparency effect driven by government disclosures effectively counters the erosion of trust fueled by conspiratorial narratives. We conclude by outlining the limitations and challenges embedded in the very idea of disclosure, a term that is ideologically and politically inflected and calls for further studies in this area.

title: Surviving Peace: What Kills Ex-Combatants after Armed Conflict
affiliations: and King's College London

detail.title: Surviving Peace: What Kills Ex-Combatants after Armed Conflict
detail.abstract: While demobilizing armed groups is a key pathway to peace, demobilized combatants often face continued violence. What kills ex-combatants? We argue that relations formed during war drive violence against ex-combatants. Continued exposure to former comrades after demobilization sustains connections that facilitate criminal reengagement and undermine legal reintegration by increasing the visibility of ex-combatants' past and related stigma. Our analysis focuses on Colombia, leveraging data on all 76,689 ex-combatants registered from 2003-2023, 6,014 of whom were killed. We find that exposure to former comrades increases the likelihood of violent death. This holds for former right-wing paramilitaries (AUC) and communist insurgents (FARC). Instrumental variable regressions, panel evidence, and causal mediation analyses support this relationship and the proposed mechanism. Qualitative interviews with ex-paramilitaries further illustrate how continued contact with former comrades generates risks of violence. These findings have important implications for demobilization policy and the sustainability of peace.

title: Governing Military Artificial Intelligence Technologies: Manufacturing War or Peace with Artificial Intelligence
affiliations: City University of Hong Kong (CityU) and

detail.title: Governing Military Artificial Intelligence Technologies: Manufacturing War or Peace with Artificial Intelligence
detail.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) technologies are reshaping national security and the future landscape of warfare. Alongside this transformation, academic discourse on military AI has gained significant traction in recent years. In response to the rapidly expanding yet fragmented scholarly discourse on military AI, this paper employs BERTopic modeling, an advanced natural language processing technique, to conduct a systematic review of military AI literature spanning over a decade (2014-2025). Based on 505 papers screened from the Web of Science (WOS) and moving back and forth between the literature and the topic modeling results, we identified 12 topics and summarized them into three spectra and six sub-themes: governance: national strategy, rules and ethics; application: regional security and conflicts, social and cultural influences; and technology: tactics, logistics. Our study generates a novel knowledge map of military AI research that provides scholars with a systematic understanding of the field's intellectual structure and evolution and offers policymakers valuable empirical insights into emerging military AI technological trends and critical governance challenges.

title: Algorithmic Screening and Access in the Gig Economy

detail.title: Algorithmic Screening and Access in the Gig Economy

publicationDetails.detailsText: Cornell SC Johnson College of Business Research Paper
publicationDetails.journalName: Cornell SC Johnson College of Business Research Paper Series

detail.abstract: Gig economy platforms face substantial uncertainty about whether dispatched workers will accept job offers—uncertainty reflecting workers’ transient circumstances rather than permanent characteristics, and one whose operational cost, in wasted capacity and delayed service, is growing as multihoming intensifies. A platform’s ability to screen for true worker availability therefore lies at the heart of marketplace efficiency and service access. Screening operates through two mechanisms: wage-setting, which generates market congestion that deters uncommitted workers through long idle times, and algorithmic profiling, which filters workers at the moment of dispatch using real-time data signals. We develop a competitive search equilibrium model characterizing how these mechanisms interact. The model identifies two screening regimes—separating (congestion-based) and pooling (algorithm-based)—and sharp transitions between them. As dispatch algorithms become more informative, they substitute for congestion-based screening: the platform optimally lowers wages and shortens idle times, but attracts a less reliable worker pool that introduces dispatch failures entirely absent under congestion-based deterrence—a tradeoff the platform willingly accepts in return for lower wage costs. Calibrated to ride-hailing data, the transition to algorithm-based screening reduces per-trip driver pay by 26% while raising platform profit by 16%. Extending the model spatially, lower expected fares and deadheading risk combine to threaten complete service collapse in lower-income areas. A profit-maximizing platform optimally subsidizes these areas to preserve the system-wide supply circulation on which its screening equilibrium depends. Because service degradation, wage suppression, and algorithmic over-rejection in lower-income areas share a common structural root, this single intervention simultaneously improves service access, wage equity, and algorithmic fairness—and raises system-wide platform profit by 14%, confirming the intervention is profit-maximizing rather than redistributive.

title: The Market for Interpretation and the Limits of Textualism
affiliations: Florida State University - College of Law

detail.title: The Market for Interpretation and the Limits of Textualism
detail.abstract:
Many courts use textualist interpretation by default for contracts where both parties are deemed sophisticated. This default misaligns with both the heterogeneous preferences of sophisticated contracting parties and contract law’s plural value commitments. There are two competing theories about the purpose of default rules. One view has it that defaults should approximate what most parties would have wanted. The other sees defaults as tools for advancing the broader aims of law, including autonomy and welfarism. The current sophistication default fails under both views.

I contend that flipping the default rule for contract interpretation for sophisticated parties from textualism to contextualism would incentivize out-of-court dispute resolution, redistribute litigation burdens away from dominant firms, and better align interpretive practice with contract law’s goals. A contextualist default reflects the autonomy value of contract law, and makes society better off, supporting contract law’s welfarist commitment.

title: The Last Paper - Agentic AI and the Governance of Empirical Finance

detail.title: The Last Paper - Agentic AI and the Governance of Empirical Finance
detail.abstract: Much of empirical finance works by searching already-realized data-decades of returns, filings, and transactions that sit in queryable databases. Agentic AI makes that search very fast. It does not make the data richer. The historical shocks, regulatory discontinuities, and natural experiments needed for credible causal inference are features of the past, not products of faster computing. The result is an asymmetry: the number of statistical tests a researcher can run is exploding, but the number of questions the data can credibly answer is not. This asymmetry has three consequences. First, candidate findings arrive faster than the profession can verify them. Second, researchers who hit dead ends-specifications that fail, identification strategies that do not work-have no reason to report them, so the next researcher wastes time rediscovering the same failure. Third, the safeguards built for slower research production-pre-registration, peer review, the paper format itself-cannot keep up. We calibrate the argument using evidence from the factor-zoo and anomaly-decay literatures, causal-design audits of corporate finance and accounting, and a new corpus of 9,437 papers from four top finance journals. The corpus contains 165 shock-based causal designs-1.8% of all papers-with heavy reuse of a small set of historical shocks. We propose three buildable responses: structured research commits that make specifications machine-readable, third-party verification using data the researcher never accessed, and a public registry of dead ends that turns failed attempts into a map of what the data cannot answer. We do not claim that causal opportunities are running out on a fixed schedule. We argue that the profession's qualitycontrol institutions were built for a slower world, and that world is ending.

title: When AI Advertises: How Advertising Disclosure Shapes Users' Trust in Generative AI

detail.title: When AI Advertises: How Advertising Disclosure Shapes Users' Trust in Generative AI

declarations.ethicsApproval: The study has benn approved by IRB.

detail.abstract: As AI providers increasingly explore advertising within generative AI systems, they face a fundamental tension between monetization and users' adoption. This research examines how, when, and why advertising disclosure in generative AI responses influences users' trust in the AI system. We argue that advertising disclosure can undermine users' trust by reducing perceived AI neutrality, and this negative effect depends on the disclosure format.When disclosure is attached to the target product that users explicitly seek in a generative AI query, it reduces both trust in the AI system and trust in the advertised product. In contrast, when disclosure is attached to a non-target product presented after an organic recommendation for the target product, it decreases trust in the advertised recommendation but does not significantly diminish trust in the AI model overall. Our claims are supported by results from three laboratory experiments. Taken together, our findings offer theoretical insights into trust formation in AI-mediated decisionmaking and provide practical guidance for the design and monetization using advertising of generative AI systems.

detail.abstract:
This technical report analyzes structural vulnerabilities and governance risks emerging in contemporary multi-model AI ecosystems. Rather than focusing on isolated model behavior, the work examines failure modes arising from interactions between multiple large language models operating under heterogeneous alignment, safety, and epistemic control regimes.

Through cross-model comparative analysis, longitudinal interaction observation, and operator-in-the-loop experimentation, the report identifies systemic risks such as epistemic containment cascades, attribution instability, semantic convergence without coordination, and governance blind spots in distributed AI systems.

The analysis situates these findings within the broader context of AI governance, socio-technical systems, and human–AI interaction, emphasizing how current safety, alignment, and evaluation frameworks may unintentionally introduce fragility when applied to high-agency, non-standard usage patterns.
Rather than proposing speculative futures, this report documents observable behaviors and architectural tensions already present in deployed AI systems. Its objective is to provide a technically grounded reference for researchers, policymakers, and system designers concerned with robustness, accountability, and governance in multi-model AI environments.

title: Cognitive Sovereignty: On the Ownership of Human Judgment in the Age of Autonomous AI

detail.title: Cognitive Sovereignty: On the Ownership of Human Judgment in the Age of Autonomous AI

declarations.declarationOfInterest: The author declares no conflicts of interest.
declarations.ethicsApproval: This paper is a theoretical and legal analysis. No human participants or personal data were involved. No ethics approval was required.
declarations.funderStatement: This research received no external funding. It was conducted independently by the author.

detail.abstract: We report on a personal experiment in which the author constructed an autonomous agent trained on their own decision-making patterns, risk evaluation criteria, and reasoning frameworks. Using years of accumulated interactions with AI systems, professional email correspondence, and domain-specific prompts designed to extract cognitive patterns, the agent was trained and deployed on Gemini Studio within a two-week period. The agent demonstrated high fidelity in replicating what decisions were made, while systematically failing to capture who makes them-the friction, doubt, and consequence-forged intuition that constitutes genuine human judgment. This gap raises unresolved questions regarding ownership, compensation, and accountability in the extraction of cognitive assets from human operators of AI systems. We document the cultural and technical mechanisms by which platforms currently extract human judgment without explicit consent or compensation, and propose a framework for cognitive sovereignty-the principle that an individual's reasoning architecture constitutes a protectable and compensable asset. We further document recent evidence that this problem extends beyond training data to posthumous identity simulation, as demonstrated by a patent approved by Meta Platforms in late 2025. We call for the establishment of verifiable standards for cognitive asset ownership and propose an open protocol for cognitive capture, certification, and compensation. This paper serves as a foundational contribution to that broader conversation.

title: Measuring Welfare Gains from Digital Variety: Evidence from App-level Time Use in China
affiliations: National Bureau of Economic Research (NBER), Nanyang Technological University (NTU) and Stanford University

detail.title: Measuring Welfare Gains from Digital Variety: Evidence from App-level Time Use in China
detail.abstract: This paper measures the welfare gains from the rapid expansion of digital apps using comprehensive app-level time-use data from China. We develop a framework in which apps are offered at zero monetary price but compete for users' time, allowing the welfare effects of new digital varieties to be inferred from reallocations of consumer attention. Applying the framework to data covering major digital apps between 2018 and 2025, we estimate that expanding digital variety raises consumer welfare by about 8 percent-roughly one-fifth of income growth. The results highlight the importance of accounting for free digital goods in welfare measurement.

title: Collective Deliberation: A Multi-Agent Framework for Fake News Analysis and Detection
affiliations: Hong Kong Polytechnic University, Hong Kong Polytechnic University and

detail.title: Collective Deliberation: A Multi-Agent Framework for Fake News Analysis and Detection
detail.abstract: The digital age has amplified challenges to information integrity on social media with the spread of fake news, threatening public discourse and democracy. Traditional content moderation methods struggle to handle the volume and complexity of fake news, a problem exacerbated by the rise of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI). Although large language models (LLMs) show promise for enhancing fake news detection, their direct application introduces risks such as hallucinations and inconsistencies. To address these challenges, this study proposes a novel LLM-based multi-agent system designed for robust fake news detection and analysis. Our framework is guided by truth-default theory (TDT) and is organized into three stages. First, a multi-agent debate mechanism generates high-quality, TDT-informed interpretive questions to scrutinize the content. Second, retrieval-augmented generation is used to produce evidence-based answers to these questions, ensuring factual grounding. Third, a classification model integrates these generated interpretive features to ensure transparent and reliable fake news detection. A performance-driven parameter optimization mechanism then continuously optimizes the question generation policy, improving the system's efficacy over time. Empirical evaluations conducted on open-source datasets, comprising human-and machine-generated fake news, demonstrate that our system significantly outperforms existing methods. This research makes several contributions. Methodologically, this study is the first to integrate deception theory into an LLM-based detection framework, facilitated by an innovative multi-agent debate mechanism. Practically, the framework supports evidence-based decision-making and provides actionable insights to social media platforms and policymakers addressing fake news in the GenAI era.

detail.abstract: There is a severe problem with personalized learning systems: fixed educational material always cannot fit the cognitive profiles and learning rates of individual learners and their areas of deficiency in knowledge. The reviewed systematic review focuses on artificial intelligence recommendation systems to design personalized and adaptive learning resources, and focuses particularly on learning analytics to serve as a base data infrastructure. Collaborative, content-based, deep learning, and knowledge graph-based approaches were tested in terms of their effectiveness in creating adaptive learning courses. Learning analytics were evaluated on the basis of their ability to record behavioral, cognitive and affective data about the learners in minute detail. Hybrid recommendation systems with the use of machine learning and semantic technologies showed high capabilities in terms of engagement with learners and retention of knowledge. The predictive accuracy of educational data mining methods was found to be of important predictive value in the performance of students and their probability of dropping out. Privacy-preserving methods and federated learning became the key instruments of the ethical implementation of AI in the learning setting. The challenges that have been identified are data sparsity, cold-start problems, algorithmic bias, and interpretability shortages in deep neural models. In this paper, key research gaps that will be listed are the cross-platform interoperability, explainable AI in education, and equity-conscious personalization. The results add a level of structure to the evidence base of the researchers, instructional designers, and education policymakers developing AI-based adaptive learning in the post-pandemic digital learning environment.

detail.abstract: This project introduces the U.S. Census’s Management and Organizational Practices Survey (MOPS) data into the employee share ownership research landscape, with the goal of investigating the role of workplace management and organizational practices in shaping the impact of broad-based employee share ownership on labor productivity at American manufacturing workplaces.  We combine data from the 2010 and 2015 Census MOPS, the American Survey of Manufactures (ASM), the US Longitudinal Business Database (LBD), and the US Department of Labor Form 5500 Pension Database.  MOPS is the largest management practices survey ever conducted of US manufacturing workplace establishments.  We show, among other results, that adopting an Employee Stock Ownership Plan (ESOP) is associated with a 5.6 to 6.7 % increase in labor productivity over 2010 to 2015, controlling for workplace management and organizational practices.

title: Learning from Repeated Internal Versus External Failures: A Dynamic Attributional Perspective
affiliations: Carnegie Mellon University, ESCP Business School and University College Dublin

detail.title: Learning from Repeated Internal Versus External Failures: A Dynamic Attributional Perspective

keywords: learning from internal versus external failures

detail.abstract: This study develops a theoretical framework explaining how organizations learn from repeated failures depending on their causal origins-internal versus external. Prior research generally assumes that once a failure's cause is identified, its learning value is fixed: internally caused failures promote learning because they are perceived as controllable, whereas externally caused failures are largely disregarded because they are seen as outside the organization's influence. We challenge this static view by proposing a dynamic attributional process in which organizations revise their interpretations of controllability as they accumulate experience with each type of failure. Specifically, we argue that internally caused failures initially stimulate learning because they are viewed as actionable, but repeated exposure can erode perceived controllability and reduce motivation to learn. In contrast, externally caused failures are initially dismissed as uncontrollable, but as they recur and reveal patterns, organizations begin to reinterpret them as manageable, thereby triggering learning and adaptation. Using 15 years of monthly U.S. airline panel data, along with qualitative interviews, we find support for the hypothesized inverted Ushaped learning curve for internal failures and the U-shaped learning curve for external failures, consistent with our dynamic attributional framework.

title: Flexible Work Arrangement Practices and Audit Quality
affiliations: University of Kentucky - Von Allmen School of Accountancy , University of Kentucky - Von Allmen School of Accountancy and University of North Carolina (UNC) at Charlotte - Department of Accounting

detail.title: Flexible Work Arrangement Practices and Audit Quality
detail.abstract: This study examines the relation between audit firm flexible work arrangement (FWA) practices and audit quality. Our examination is motivated by recent debates regarding the potential tradeoffs of FWAs and concerns from audit regulators about the potential impact of FWAs on audit quality. We use Revelio Labs sentiment data to capture audit firm employees' perceptions of their firms' FWA practices, since prior work suggests that employee perceptions align with how FWA practices are implemented in the workplace. We find evidence suggesting that more favorable FWA perceptions are associated with lower audit quality on average. Results of additional tests suggest that the relation between FWA practices and audit quality varies based on individual auditor characteristics, engagement complexity, and the potential mismatch between audit firm and client firm FWA practices. In sum, our study offers timely evidence on the potential consequences of FWA practices for the audit profession.

This article explains we should expect to see more companies on the brink of defaulting on financial obligations they took on when interest rates were very low, for example bonds.  To the extent that past is prologue, iconic American brands and foreign registered companies will seek bankruptcy protection - if they seek bankruptcy protection - outside of the jurisdictions where companies have centers of main interest/nerve centers/operations/land/employees.

detail.title: On the Origins of Scaling in Urban Retail
detail.abstract: Cities serve as a central nexus of innovation, economic activity, and social interaction. Researchers have established urban scaling laws to characterize socioeconomic and infrastructural indicators such as GDP and road length, yet the mechanisms governing scaling behaviour in the retail sector remain elusive. Leveraging datasets from the United States and France, we investigate the structural relationship between retail infrastructure and urban development. We find that the three major retail formats-supercenters, supermarkets, and convenience stores-do not follow a uniform scaling law but exhibit heterogeneous behaviour: supercenters scale sublinearly, supermarkets scale approximately linearly, and convenience stores scale superlinearly with city population. We develop a unified theoretical framework that decomposes consumer demand into routine household purchases and mobility-driven spatial interactions, and derives these distinct scaling exponents from differences in market positioning and operational cost structure across retail formats. Model predictions fall within the 95% confidence intervals of empirical estimates in both the United States and France, validating the framework across two independent retail systems. This work bridges urban science and operations management, advancing our understanding of the co-evolution of retail infrastructure and urban structure.

title: Post-Quantum Negligence: Applying the Learned Hand Formula to Organizational Liability for Quantum Computing Threats

detail.title: Post-Quantum Negligence: Applying the Learned Hand Formula to Organizational Liability for Quantum Computing Threats
detail.abstract:
The cryptographic algorithms protecting virtually all digital commerce, communication, and data storage will be rendered obsolete by quantum computing. Adversaries are already exploiting this inevitability through “Harvest Now, Decrypt Later” strategies—intercepting and storing encrypted data today for decryption once quantum computers become operational—and through “Harvest Now, Forge Later” strategies that will enable the forgery of digital signatures undermining authentication, code signing, and legal instruments. The National Institute of Standards and Technology finalized post-quantum cryptographic standards in August 2024. The European Union, the United Kingdom, Australia, Canada, and the G7 have issued binding mandates or formal migration guidance. Yet no U.S. private-sector regulation currently requires adoption of quantum-resistant cryptography. Nor has legal scholarship applied established negligence frameworks to the organizational liability these threats create.

This Article fills that gap by proposing two original frameworks. The first, the “Mosca Hand Model,” integrates a cryptographic risk assessment tool—Mosca’s Theorem, which quantifies the relationship between data shelf life, migration time, and the timeline to quantum decryption—with the Learned Hand Formula, the foundational economic test for negligence. The synthesis transforms the abstract question of quantum foreseeability into a quantifiable, organization-specific analysis: whether the burden of migrating to post-quantum cryptography is less than the probability of quantum-enabled harm multiplied by the magnitude of resulting loss. Using expert probability estimates from the December 2024 Quantum Threat Timeline Report, the Article demonstrates that this analysis yields concrete, documentable results that courts, boards, and regulators can apply.

The second framework, the “Goldilocks Duty,” addresses the bilateral risk inherent in cryptographic migration. Organizations face legal exposure both from migrating too slowly (continued vulnerability to quantum attack and accumulating HNDL exposure) and from migrating too recklessly (operational failures from premature adoption of immature standards). The Article proposes “deliberate speed” as the appropriate standard of care—urgent but not reckless, methodical but not dilatory—and identifies the factors courts will weigh in evaluating organizational conduct along this spectrum.

The Article further establishes that quantum threats are already legally foreseeable under existing negligence standards, drawing on international regulatory action, the T.J. Hooper principle that industry custom does not define the standard of care, and a negligence per se analysis demonstrating that existing statutory requirements for “reasonable” security may already encompass quantum-resilient cryptography. It connects the tort analysis to corporate governance obligations—including Caremark oversight duties, the Business Judgment Rule, and SEC cybersecurity disclosure requirements—and proposes a minimum defensible position that corporate counsel can implement immediately. The Article concludes that the critical distinction in future quantum-related litigation will not be between organizations that had completed migration and those that had not, but between organizations that had governed and those that had not.

title: SUPPLY CHAIN MANAGEMENT AND OPERATIONAL EFFICIENCY: A STUDY OF CURRENCY POLYMER, KANO STATE, NIGERIA

detail.title: SUPPLY CHAIN MANAGEMENT AND OPERATIONAL EFFICIENCY: A STUDY OF CURRENCY POLYMER, KANO STATE, NIGERIA
detail.abstract: Supply chain inefficiencies and ineffective inventory management pose significant challenges to production cycle time and cost reduction in manufacturing firms. This study examined the relationship between supply chain management and operational efficiency using Currency Polymer, Bompai, Kano State as the study area. The objectives of the study were to examine the relationship between supply chain integration and production cycle time in Currency Polymer, Bompai, Kano State and to assess the relationship between inventory management and cost reduction in Currency Polymer, Bompai, Kano State. A quantitative research design was adopted, utilizing a structured questionnaire for data collection. The instrument was validated through expert review and its reliability was ascertained using Cronbach's alpha method. The study population comprised employees from supply chain-related departments, with a sample size of 139 respondents selected using a stratified random sampling technique. Data were analyzed using multiple correlation and regression analysis in SPSS. Findings revealed that Supply Chain Integration (SCI) components exhibited a strong positive correlation with Product Cycle Time (PCT) (r-values ranging from 0.789 to 0.874, p < 0.05), affirming that integration significantly improves production efficiency. Similarly, Inventory Management (IM) variables correlated positively with Cost Reduction (CR), with inventory optimization (r = 0.854, p < 0.05) having the highest impact. The study concluded that effective Supply Chain Integration (SCI) enhances production speed, while Inventory Management (IM) practices significantly influence Cost Reduction (CR). It recommended enhanced technology adoption for SCI, improved inventory tracking systems, optimized procurement processes, and continuous workforce training to sustain operational efficiency and cost-effectiveness.

title: Privacy-Preserving Data Processing and Federated Learning in Cloud Systems

detail.title: Privacy-Preserving Data Processing and Federated Learning in Cloud Systems
detail.abstract: Cloud computing has transformed the way organizations store, process, and analyze data. However, the widespread adoption of cloud systems raises significant concerns regarding privacy, security, and compliance. This research investigates privacy-preserving data processing in cloud environments, with a particular focus on federated learning, which enables decentralized machine learning without transferring sensitive data to a central server. The study examines the integration of privacy-preserving mechanisms such as differential privacy, homomorphic encryption, and secure multiparty computation, and evaluates their impact on model accuracy, computational cost, and system efficiency. Key findings demonstrate that federated learning, when combined with these techniques, reduces privacy risks while maintaining high model performance. Furthermore, AI-driven orchestration and agentic frameworks provide autonomous monitoring, root cause analysis, and optimization of cloud resources, enhancing the resilience and efficiency of distributed systems. The study concludes that adopting privacy-preserving federated learning frameworks in cloud systems offers a scalable, secure, and effective solution for modern organizations processing sensitive data (Sarraf & Pal, 2026; Maheshkar, 2026).

title: Governance-Aware Dynamic Resource Allocation in Distributed Computing Environments Using Adaptive Centrality-Entropy Index with Oscillation Suppression
affiliations: University of the Cumberlands

detail.title: Governance-Aware Dynamic Resource Allocation in Distributed Computing Environments Using Adaptive Centrality-Entropy Index with Oscillation Suppression
detail.abstract: Modern distributed computing environments suffer from resource thrashing, cascading failures, and inefficient allocation due to reliance on static utilization thresholds. This paper presents a governance-aware dynamic resource allocation framework integrating a novel Centrality-Entropy Index (CEI) with adaptive weight recalibration, oscillation suppression via hysteresis windows, fault propagation probability modeling, and pre-modification k-hop simulation. Unlike conventional autoscaling that reacts to instantaneous CPU or memory metrics, the proposed system reconstructs sustained workload behavior through longitudinal telemetry analysis, incorporates mission-criticality and disaster recovery dependencies into allocation decisions, and validates modifications against a dependency graph before execution. Empirical validation in a production cloud environment demonstrated sustained cost savings of 27% ($6,000/month from $22,000 baseline), 35-40% reduction in scaling oscillation events, and 18-22% improvement in compute utilization efficiency. The framework is platform-agnostic, operating on standardized telemetry across AWS, Azure, Google Cloud, and Kubernetes environments. A provisional patent application (USPTO No. 63/999,378) has been filed for the system architecture.

title: The Carrying Capacity of Leadership: A Dynamic Systems Model of Executive Sustainability

detail.title: The Carrying Capacity of Leadership: A Dynamic Systems Model of Executive Sustainability
detail.abstract: We model leadership effectiveness as a coupled dynamical system in which accumulated human capital, organizational complexity, and energetic capacity coevolve. The central mechanism is endogenous capital-complexity coupling: professional success generates coordination demands that deplete the vitality required for sustained strategic impact. Using a two-dimensional ODE system, we derive a critical carrying capacity threshold and identify conditions under which leaders converge to a stable low-vitality trap—the "zombie equilibrium"—with attenuated strategic contribution. Leadership effectiveness is energy-gated: accumulated capital must be deployed through finite vitality to produce impact. We identify complementary organizational levers—architectural redesign and recovery enhancement—show their effectiveness depends on distinct mathematical channels, and characterize the zombie equilibrium as a welfare-reducing market failure. Simulation, bifurcation analysis, and robustness checks support the framework's core predictions.

title: A Study on the Status and Practical Role of Fire Departmental Rules in China's Fire Protection Legal Basis System

detail.title: A Study on the Status and Practical Role of Fire Departmental Rules in China's Fire Protection Legal Basis System
detail.abstract: With the ongoing legalization of fire safety governance and the restructuring of China's emergency management system, frontline enforcement and collaborative, society-wide governance increasingly require refined and operational normative support. As an intermediate layer between statutes and enforcement practice, fire-sector departmental rules are subordinate to higher-level law, execution-oriented, and technically specialized; they translate general legal principles into workable requirements for unit-based fire safety management, supervision and inspection, fire investigation, and the regulation of social fire technical services. Drawing on literature review, normative interpretation, and institutional mapping, this paper outlines the hierarchy of China's fire protection legal basis system, clarifies the rank and boundaries of legal effect of departmental rules under the Legislation Law and the Regulation on Procedures for Formulating Rules, and systematically examines key current rules-including those on unit fire safety management, fire supervision and inspection, fire accident investigation, social fire technical services, registered fire engineers, and high-rise civil building fire safety-by tracing their policy context, core provisions, and practical functions. The findings suggest that departmental rules play a crucial role in operationalizing the responsibility framework of the Fire Protection Law, standardizing enforcement procedures, and enhancing predictability in governance. Further improvement is needed in coordination with higher-level laws and local norms, as well as in post-implementation evaluation and timely revision mechanisms.

title: Optimal Location Of Aerial Firefighting Resources To Maximize Coverage: A Case Study Of Greece

detail.title: Optimal Location Of Aerial Firefighting Resources To Maximize Coverage: A Case Study Of Greece
detail.abstract: Wildfires affect many different regions of the world having many negative consequences on humans, wildlife, and the economy. Aerial resources play a crucial role in combating wildfires and an effective resource location plan is of paramount importance for enhancing their utilization. To this effect, several factors should be considered such as the fire hazard levels of each area, the specificities of the aerial firefighting fleet, the availability of airbases (airports and heliports), etc. In the present study, a decision support model is developed, under realistic assumptions and driven by practical considerations, to dictate the optimal assignment of aerial firefighting resources to the available facilities, in order to maximize the expected coverage. To demonstrate the applicability of the model, Greece is employed as a case study, considering multi-year wildfire statistics, the Greek aerial firefighting fleet, and the licensed airbases in Greek territory. Finally, the effectiveness of the model is evaluated through a comparison between the optimal solution and an existing location plan of Greek aerial firefighting resources.

title: Sustainable Manufacturing: Multi-Objective Optimization of Production and Environmental Impact

detail.title: Sustainable Manufacturing: Multi-Objective Optimization of Production and Environmental Impact
detail.abstract: This study examines sustainable manufacturing through the lens of multi-objective optimization, focusing on the simultaneous improvement of production efficiency and reduction of environmental impact in industrial systems. Drawing on prior empirical studies, optimization frameworks, and applied industrial analytics, the research synthesizes evidence on how multi-objective decision models outperform single-objective production strategies in balancing economic and environmental goals (Adeparusi and Ajenifuja; Chen et al.; Khan and Gupta). The findings indicate that multi-objective optimization approaches consistently reduce carbon emissions, energy intensity, and environmental risk while maintaining stable or improved production outputs (Orion and Imogen; Kumar and Kumar). However, the results also reveal trade-offs, including short-term cost increases and operational complexity when environmental constraints are tightened (AdeparuBhalani). The study concludes that sustainable manufacturing cannot be achieved through isolated efficiency optimization alone and that multi-objective frameworks aligned with Industry 5.0 principles offer a more resilient and responsible pathway for industrial development (Chen et al.; Ajenifuja and Adeparusi 2024b).

detail.abstract: Enterprises are rapidly shifting from human-interpreted dashboards to Autonomous Analytical Entities (AAE) that execute decisions directly on production systems. This paper proposes the Autonomous Analytical Coherence (AAC) framework, centered on an Analytical Control Plane (ACP) that inserts a mandatory, machine-enforced governance layer between AAEs and decentralized data products. The ACP mandates Agentic Data Contracts (ADC) as runtime dependencies and enforces Kullback-Leibler (KL) divergence-based drift checks within Trusted Execution Environments (TEE) to safeguard both analytical coherence and data sovereignty. Simulation-based experiments across finance and logistics workloads indicate that AAC reduces erroneous autonomous transactions by 77% compared with uncoordinated agent deployments, with only a 25 ms median increase in latency. These results demonstrate that treating governance as a runtime dependency is a practical path toward safe, high-stakes autonomous analytics in enterprise data meshes.

detail.abstract: Research generally depicts automation as deskilling for entry-level workers, yet this may not always be the case. Through our two-year, nationwide, multi-sited ethnographic study of warehousing, we show how some workers built more complex skills after the arrival of new technology. They did so by addressing problems arising from misalignments between new technologies and established workflows, thereby developing the capacity to intervene in the systems surrounding their narrow tasks. But for these capacities to develop into valued skills, their problem-solving had to be recognized by managers, who controlled access to opportunities to solve organization-level problems. Our findings underscore the powerful barriers to onthe-job skill building in contemporary low-wage workplaces, while showing how technological change can create opportunities for some workers to broaden their skills. This work advances our understanding of how workers build skill during technological change and suggests pathways for improving talent development opportunities in low-wage work.

title: PLC and Machine Vision Integration for Eco-Friendly Quality Control in Manufacturing

detail.title: PLC and Machine Vision Integration for Eco-Friendly Quality Control in Manufacturing
detail.abstract: This study investigates the integration of Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs) and machine vision systems as a unified framework for eco-friendly quality control in modern manufacturing environments. The research designed and evaluated an integrated PLC-machine vision architecture capable of real-time defect detection, automated control adjustment, and energy optimization. Using a controlled production simulation environment, performance metrics, including detection accuracy, scrap reduction, operational downtime, and estimated energy consumption were assessed. The findings show that integrating machine vision with PLC-based control logic improves defect detection accuracy, reduces material waste, and lowers energy consumption compared to traditional inspection systems. Unexpectedly, energy savings exceeded defect reduction improvements, suggesting that adaptive shutdown logic and dynamic control sequencing contributed significantly to environmental efficiency. The study concludes that PLC-machine vision integration offers a scalable and sustainable approach to quality assurance aligned with Industry 4.0 principles and environmentally responsible manufacturing frameworks. These findings extend prior research on predictive maintenance, digital twins, and environmental modeling by positioning quality control not only as an operational necessity but also as a sustainability strategy (Ajenifuja and Adeparusi 2023; Adeparusi and Ajenifuja 2025).

title: When Terminal Value Goes to Zero: Artificial Intelligence, Application-Specific Integrated Robots, and the Compression of Economic Lifespans
affiliations: Independent

detail.title: When Terminal Value Goes to Zero: Artificial Intelligence, Application-Specific Integrated Robots, and the Compression of Economic Lifespans
detail.abstract:
Traditional discounted cash flow (DCF) models assume firms generate cash flows across extended horizons, with terminal value often representing the majority of estimated firm worth. This paper proposes a duration-centered mechanism in which artificial intelligence (AI) alters firm value by increasing the hazard rate governing the survival of competitive advantage, rather than solely through productivity or margin effects.

Current discourse around artificial intelligence (AI) focuses primarily on productivity and margin effects. This paper proposes a different mechanism: AI may compress the expected duration of competitive advantage. We introduce a lifespan-adjusted valuation framework incorporating survival probability into discounted cash flows. Extending an analogy from computing, we define application-specific integrated robots (ASIR) as narrowly deployed autonomous systems operating within structured environments. Using a GPU-based analogy, ASIR deployment represents an automation threshold where deterministic workflows shift from bespoke "CPU-like" human coordination to modular parallel execution that scales as a platform, potentially triggering nonlinear valuation shifts. The framework distinguishes deterministic and probabilistic output domains, introduces capital elasticity as a driver of hazard rates, and presents a Terminal Value Fragility Curve describing nonlinear duration risk. Implications for capital markets, strategy, and labor structure are discussed.

title: On the Design of an AI-Human Service System with Strategic Customers: Should AI be mandated?
affiliations: University of Rochester - Simon Business School and University of Rochester - Simon Business School

detail.title: On the Design of an AI-Human Service System with Strategic Customers: Should AI be mandated?
detail.abstract: Problem definition: AI agents are increasingly deployed across industries, yet their limited proficiency remains a key concern. In many services, customers are first interacting with AI agents, and are routed to a human agent only if the AI agent failed to serve them. However, a growing debate about mandating AI services has recently emerged, bringing the U.S. Congress to float bills aiming to grant consumers the right to choose human service directly. Methodology/results: Motivated by this realistic setting, we develop a game-theoretical queueing framework to compare customer equilibrium behavior and system performance under two operational designs: an AI-mandate model and a customer-choice model. In both models, customers who attend the AI service are routed to a human service if their case is beyond the capability of the AI agent. Our comparison provides conditions under which each model performs better in terms of throughput and social welfare. Specifically, we consider the impact of the AI proficiency level and demand level on the optimal model choice. Managerial implications: Our analysis reveals several non-intuitive results. We find that for a given proficiency level, selecting the model that maximizes the throughput does not depend on the demand level, signaling operational convenience. In addition, when demand is relatively high, we show that the choice model requires a higher AI proficiency level than the AI-mandate model to achieve maximal throughput. In term of social welfare, our result reveals that granting customer choice can backfire when AI proficiency level is relatively high. We further show the robustness of our results in the case where some of the customers are reluctant toward the AI service.

title: THE 4-STAGE GROWTH MODEL An Enterprise Architecture Framework for Small-Business Transformation

detail.title: THE 4-STAGE GROWTH MODEL An Enterprise Architecture Framework for Small-Business Transformation
detail.abstract: Small businesses frequently encounter growth plateaus that persist despite strong products, capable leadership, and sustained managerial effort. Conventional explanations attribute these stalls to execution failures, resource constraints, or inadequate planning, yet fail to explain why growth repeatedly falters as organizational complexity increases. This article advances a developmental explanation: early growth unfolds through a sequence of natural developmental phases, each defined by an enterprise architecture capable of supporting higher levels of managerial sophistication, coordination, and structural integration. The article introduces the 4-Stage Growth Model, which conceptualizes growth stages as natural developmental architectures-integrated configurations of market logic, organizational design, leadership systems, operating processes, and planning horizons that evolve with complexity. Eight interdependent architectural dimensions are specified and held constant across stages, enabling diagnosis of the enterprise's current developmental configuration and deliberate design of the future-state architecture required at the next growth horizon. Growth stalls are explained as outcomes of developmental misalignment and path dependence: architectural commitments formed in earlier phases enable local coherence while constraining advancement to higher levels of complexity. Rather than relying on illustrative cases, the article develops a theory-driven account of stage transitions as enterprise repositioning events, identifying core mechanisms of transition stress, predictable failure modes, boundary conditions, and testable propositions. By reframing growth plateaus as consequences of developmental architecture and managerial cognition limits rather than generalized managerial failure, the 4-Stage Growth Model provides a parsimonious yet extensible foundation for future empirical research on small-business growth, enterprise design, and leadership in complex organizations.

title: From Syntax to Semantics: The Rise of the Taste-Based Economy and Viral Creation Loops in Intent-Driven Software Generation

detail.title: From Syntax to Semantics: The Rise of the Taste-Based Economy and Viral Creation Loops in Intent-Driven Software Generation
detail.abstract: The emergence of "Vibe Coding"-a paradigm where developers guide AI systems through natural language intent rather than explicit syntax-represents a fundamental shift in software engineering. This transformation is not merely technical but economic: as Large Language Models (LLMs) commoditize programming skills, the locus of value creation shifts from syntactic mastery to semantic judgment, or what we term "taste." This paper introduces the Taste-Based Economy framework to explain how early-stage startups can build sustainable competitive advantages when marginal production costs approach zero. Through a multiple case study analysis of three leading AI-native development platforms-Cursor, Replit, and Lovable-we identify three distinct Go-to-Market (GTM) archetypes: Flow-Led Growth, Remix-Led Growth, and Creation-Led Growth. Our findings reveal that traditional technology moats are dissolving, replaced by new barriers centered on curation capability and viral creation loops. We introduce the concept of "Intent Bandwidth" to measure human-AI communication efficiency and propose a "Creativity Multiplier" metric for quantifying viral growth in generative software markets. This research contributes to marketing theory by extending Bourdieu's cultural capital framework to AI-native markets and offers practical implications for founders, venture capitalists, and platform designers navigating the post-code economy.

title: Late-Imperial Governance Fiscal Concentration and Extraordinary Taxation California Case

detail.title: Late-Imperial Governance Fiscal Concentration and Extraordinary Taxation California Case

declarations.declarationOfInterest: Continuing the journey :)

detail.abstract:
Why would a wealthy, high-capacity jurisdiction resort to an extraordinary, one-time wealth levy rather than broad, stable taxation? This paper argues that such policies are not primarily ideological choices but structural responses to fiscal stress. I introduce a simple model of “late-imperial governance,” in which revenue becomes concentrated in a small, mobile elite while public obligations expand and the broader tax base remains constrained. Under these conditions, governments increasingly substitute discretionary and targeted extraction for rule-based taxation, relying on extraordinary levies, retroactive tools, and narrow assessments to stabilize commitments that exceed normal revenue capacity.

The model generates observable indicators: reliance on elite taxpayers, heightened fiscal volatility, growing beneficiary constituencies relative to net contributors, and episodic or “temporary” measures aimed at relatively immobile capital. I validate the model historically using the Western Roman Empire, where fiscal concentration, expanding obligations, and extraordinary extraction preceded the gradual hollowing of central authority. I then apply the framework to contemporary California, characterized by heavy dependence on high-income and capital-gains taxation, pronounced boom–bust revenue cycles, expanding social commitments, and institutional limits on broadening its tax base.

Using California’s proposed 2026 Billionaire Tax Act as a case study, I argue that the policy’s significance lies less in projected revenue than in what it signals: a shift from general, predictable taxation toward discretionary, targeted extraction. This shift is consistent with late-imperial dynamics and predicts avoidance behavior, increased policy uncertainty, and longer-term fiscal fragility. The analysis reframes the debate away from partisan or moral interpretations and toward institutional incentives, suggesting that late-imperial governance patterns can emerge within modern democratic and sub-national settings. The framework offers a portable diagnostic tool for evaluating fiscal sustainability in other high-obligation, revenue-concentrated jurisdictions.

detail.title: The Impact of Tourism on Local Communities in the Maros Pangkep Geoaprk Area, Indonesia
detail.abstract: This study aims to provide an overview of how tourism, in a global context, influences the socio-cultural life of local communities in the Indonesian Geopark Area, using the Rammang-Rammang tourist attraction in the Maros-Pangkep Geopark as a case study. This research employed qualitative methods with an ethnographic approach. Data were collected through in-depth interviews, participant observation, and documentation involving local residents, tourism managers, and community leaders. The results indicate that tourism has driven changes in various complex aspects, such as improvements in physical infrastructure, diversification of livelihoods, changes in mindsets and behaviors, the creation of social disparities, and the erosion of local wisdom. These changes demonstrate that tourism has had both positive and negative impacts on local communities in the Maros-Pangkep Geopark Area. In conclusion, tourism development has become a major force for socio-cultural change. These changes are not limited to physical and economic aspects, but also deeply impact the social structure, values, and cultural practices of the community. These changes reflect the workings of modernity through the intervention of external actors, transforming the community's living space while opening access to mobility, information, and new economic opportunities.

detail.abstract: The Transformed Capacity Systems Framework™ (TCSF™) was developed as a macro-level diagnostic architecture for identifying structural misalignment in institutions-locating where governance design produces divergence between stated intent and realized outcomes, and making those divergences traceable, nameable, and addressable. This working paper documents a formal theoretical extension of that diagnostic architecture into what TCSF™ now designates as a governance maturation model. The extension emerges from two intersecting developments: first, the applied demonstration of TCSF™ in the Pennsylvania Medicaid managed care context, which surfaced live institutional dynamics that the existing conceptual vocabulary did not yet fully name; and second, a series of collegial exchanges in professional discourse that independently arrived at structural formulations consistent with TCSF™'s diagnostic logic-without the benefit of the framework's language. Both developments revealed the same gap: TCSF™ had diagnosed where institutions fail to receive structural signals, but had not yet formally theorized the conditions that prevent signal reception, the architectural mechanisms that route signals to the institutional periphery, or the governance properties required for listening to become accountable in real time. This paper introduces five formal conceptual extensions to TCSF™: the Reception Gap™, Signal Peripheralization™, the Governance Radius™, Architectural Transparency™, and the Open Architecture Phase™. Each is defined, situated within TCSF™'s existing framework architecture, and illustrated through reference to the Pennsylvania Medicaid case. Together, they constitute the theoretical basis for TCSF™'s governance maturation model-a progression from institutional diagnosis to structurally transparent, real-time, accountable governance listening.

detail.abstract: In the textile sector, employee turnover is a major concern that impacts productivity, morale, and operational efficiency. The failure of traditional ways to address this issue has led to the investigation of novel approaches. This study employs machine learning approaches to estimate employee attrition trends and evaluate real-time data for India Trimmings Private Limited. Businesses can promote stability and profitability in the India Trimmings Private Limited by implementing proactive retention techniques by recognizing the variables that contribute to turnover. model to identify attrition patterns, understanding how turnover affects organizational dynamics, and suggesting retention tactics. A sample of 408 employees, representing a range of organizational aspects and demographic groups, is investigated using a cross-sectional design and quantitative approach. Structured digital surveys are used in data collecting to get details on department, salary, advancement opportunities, experience, and attrition rate. The study is guided by theoretical frameworks of motivation, work satisfaction, and organizational commitment. These frameworks frame hypotheses regarding factors such as age, experience, departmental variances, wage levels, promotions, and job satisfaction. These departments are affected by a variety of factors, such as years of employment, education level, compensation, transportation, and work satisfaction. Targeted engagement programs, pay raises, creating a happy workplace, and individualized development opportunities are some of the recommendations. To sum up, attrition is greatly impacted by departmental characteristics, payment, and employee demographics. Developing plans to deal with these issues is crucial to keeping employees motivated and lowering attrition. Data-driven insights enable ongoing policy modifications and monitoring, guaranteeing long-term organizational performance and promoting stability and expansion in India Trimmings Private Limited.

detail.title: Between Adam Smith's Self-Love and the Impartial Spectator: Ādamiyyah as a Moral Bridge in Human Conscience
detail.abstract: This article proposes a novel moral synthesis between Adam Smith's Enlightenment conception of the impartial spectator and the Abrahamic concept of Ādamiyyah. It argues that while Smith's theory offers a robust model of internal moral regulation, its reliance on socially constructed norms leaves it vulnerable to moral relativism and cultural fragmentation. In contrast, Ādamiyyah, rooted in Qur'anic anthropology, provides a fixed ontological foundation for human dignity, affirming rights and duties by virtue of being human. Through a comparative philosophical methodology, this paper demonstrates that Ādamiyyah can validate self-regard as sacred and universal, while also anchoring the impartial spectator in a transcendent framework of accountability. Ibn Khaldūn's notion of wāziʿ min anfusihim, the internal restraining power, offers an applied articulation of this synthesis. It mirrors Smith's impartial spectator as a mechanism of self-regulation, yet grounds it in the Adamic dignity of Ādamiyyah, where moral restraint links the self to both divine accountability and social order. The article further employs the metaphor of the fixed-point theorem from mathematics to conceptualize Ādamiyyah as an invariant moral constant, stabilizing ethical reasoning across cultural and technological transformations. By addressing both individual moral formation and institutional justice, this framework resolves the micro-macro divide in ethics. The paper concludes by proposing that this integration contributes to the emerging discourse on "Rooted Futures," a call to design inclusive, ethically grounded futures by drawing on the enduring insights of classical moral traditions, and to renew the Adamic covenant of human dignity that signifies the primordial moral bond between humanity and God vertically, and among human beings horizontally. Reclaiming this covenant not only restores a global moral order grounded in justice, equality, and the inviolability of every person, but also provides the impartial spectator with the transcendent moral anchor it lacked, thereby closing the gap between self-regard and universal moral responsibility.

detail.abstract: This work studies the stabilization of nonlinear transport systems subject to super-linear feedback. In deterministic regimes, such dynamics exhibit Riccati-type gradient amplification that can destabilize the transport field. We introduce stochastic transport perturbations through the Stochastic Advection by Lie Transport (SALT) framework and analyze the resulting Lagrangian flow. By converting the Stratonovich formulation to Itô form, we show that stochastic transport generates an emergent deterministic second-order spatial operator. This operator acts as an effective viscosity term that introduces a nonnegative dissipation channel for the transported field. Under mild nondegeneracy conditions on the transport covariance, we prove that this noise-induced operator suppresses gradient amplification in expectation. The result establishes a mechanism of stochastic regularization in nonlinear transport systems whereby transport-level stochasticity produces endogenous stabilization without modifying the deterministic drift.

The principal objectives should address major global concerns and Environmental Social Governance, including climate change, population growth, and the development of a universal framework of environmental principles and laws applicable to all earthborn 1 creatures. This would facilitate responsible anthropogenic initiatives focused on the care, maintenance, and management of life on Earth. The establishment of a World Body with Tier 1 status, senior to the United Nations, and grounded in the principles of Biological Diversity-as exemplified by the Protocol on Environmental Protection to the Antarctic Treaty-is recommended, and to be based on the five major continents. Such a world body should incorporate a structured suite of Environmental Impact Assessment master handbooks, serving as effective tools for monitoring and controlling global environmental processes. Crucially, this organization must address current gaps in United Nations responsibilities, including the failings and shortcomings. It must embrace the creation of a comprehensive, structured Total Renewable Energy Master Plan for the long-term sustainability of the planet, to be used for peaceful purposes, as per Chapter 1 of the UN Charter. detail.abstract: This paper examines the productivity impact of menstruation-related presenteeism within labour-intensive sectors and proposes a behaviourally informed workplace policy intervention for Tamil Nadu’s MSME ecosystem. detail.abstract: This paper investigates how new borrowers expand their credit access. In particular, we examine the role that consumers’ credit choices, not just repayment behavior, play in building their credit histories. Using credit bureau data, we document that incumbent lenders typically increase credit limits for borrowers who open additional credit cards. This effect is especially pronounced for new borrowers. Our interpretation of this evidence is that lenders perceive credit offered by other lenders as revealing favorable information about the borrower. We build a novel model consistent with this hypothesis and show that the model’s predictions are consistent with the data.

detail.title: Expert Patients’ Use of Avoidable Health Care
detail.abstract: We measure whether expert patients – those trained as physicians and nurses – have fewer emergency department visits and the reasons for these differences. Relative to similar patients physicians and nurses had 19.8% and 5.1% fewer ED visits, principally due to fewer avoidable visits. The differences in avoidable visits between physicians and other patients were largest for diagnoses commonly requiring prescriptions, which physicians often self-prescribed. Our results suggest that improving access to prescriptions for acute symptoms, more than improving patient education, may reduce avoidable health care.

detail.title: Educational climate, perception, and relationship with depression, anxiety, stress, and academic burnout in medical students
detail.abstract: Objectives: To analyze the association between medical students' perception of the educational climate and their levels of depression, anxiety, stress, and academic burnout, and to evaluate the potential effectiveness of volunteering and educational trips in improving this perception.Methodology: Observational, cross-sectional study conducted at Francisco de Vitoria University (Madrid, Spain) from March to May 2023. A total of 558 medical students (1st–6th year) completed electronic questionnaires (response rate: 77%). Instruments included the Dundee Ready Educational Environment Measure (DREEM), the Depression-Anxiety-Stress Scales (DASS-21), and the Maslach Burnout Inventory-General Survey for Students (MBI-GS-S). Sociodemographic data and participation in volunteer/travel activities were collected. Spearman correlations and multivariate regression models were applied.Results: Mean DREEM score was 132.6 (SD=19.9), indicating a "more positive than negative" climate. High or risk burnout was present in 35.4% of students (exhaustion: 77.2%, cynicism: 19.9%, low efficacy: 39.6%). Significant negative correlations were found between educational climate and depression (Rho=-0.48), anxiety (Rho=-0.37), stress (Rho=-0.41), and burnout (Rho=-0.39). Students who participated in volunteering/educational trips reported significantly higher DREEM scores (137.1 vs. 128.6; p<0.001). The final regression model (adjusted R²=0.481) included all DASS-21 and MBI-GS-S domains, academic year, residence, and volunteer/travel activities.Conclusions: Poorer perception of educational climate is strongly associated with higher burnout and emotional distress in medical students. Volunteering and educational trips may improve this perception. Periodic evaluation of educational climate is recommended.
